# Results — Study 826 (Treasury Duration BAB)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Frazzini & Pedersen (2014): low-beta assets earn higher risk-adjusted returns, so a
**betting-against-beta** book (long low-beta legs levered to unit beta, short high-beta
legs, beta-neutral) earns a positive alpha; documented across asset classes including the
US-Treasury curve by maturity. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python
examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `e423191a2863` (five-ETF
close panel). Stamped run as-of 2026-06-30 — no partial months.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`), **5 iShares Treasury ETFs** — SHY, IEI, IEF, TLH, TLT — 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** overlapping rows |
| Universe | a fixed five-ETF ladder of the Treasury curve by maturity (SHY 1-3y → TLT 20y+), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Factor | the **equal-weight mean** of the five daily returns — a single "duration factor" all five load on |
| Signal | each ETF's **trailing-252-day beta** to the duration factor (`Cov(r_i,f)/Var(f)`), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Book | each day rank the five ETFs by beta; **long the low-beta legs** (rank-weighted, levered to unit factor beta `1/β_L`), **short the high-beta legs** (levered to unit factor beta `1/β_H`); `BAB = (r_L−rf)/β_L − (r_H−rf)/β_H`, beta-neutral by construction (`rf≈0` daily) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: beta through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges one-way cost × turnover of the levered weights; the short leg pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily BAB; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the levered legs; a factor-regression alpha + residual beta; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The five-ETF ladder is a *design choice*: no
delisted Treasury fund is silently omitted (these five have traded continuously since 2007-10),
but restricting to a clean maturity ladder is itself a selection, disclosed here.

## The beta ladder — betas rise monotonically with maturity

| ETF | SHY (1-3y) | IEI (3-7y) | IEF (7-10y) | TLH (10-20y) | TLT (20y+) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| avg trailing-252d β to factor | 0.123 | 0.470 | 0.911 | 1.402 | 2.094 |

The duration factor cleanly orders the curve — SHY is the low-beta (short-duration) leg, TLT
the high-beta (long-duration) leg — so the BAB book longs SHY/IEI (levered up) and shorts
TLH/TLT.

## The headline — Frazzini-Pedersen BAB return

Daily beta-neutral BAB (n = **3,894** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **BAB (long low-β levered − short high-β levered)** | **+1.31 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+2.50** |
| one-sample *t* | +2.37 |
| gross Sharpe | 0.60 |
| levered-low leg / levered-high leg | +2.00 bps / +0.69 bps (Welch *t* = +1.18) |
| factor-regression alpha (NW *t*) | +1.32 bps/day (+2.51) |
| residual beta to factor | **−0.007** (beta-neutral, as designed) |
| β_lo / β_hi → gross leverage | 0.238 / 1.864 → **5.04×** |

At face value the BAB clears the bar: **+1.31 bps/day, NW *t* = +2.50**, right sign, and the
book is genuinely beta-neutral (residual β ≈ 0). The two robustness checks below show why that
face value is misleading.

## Placebo — is the beta signal doing the work, or the leverage cage?

Keep the beta-rank weights and the `1/β` leverage fixed; permute **which ETF's return feeds
each leg** (beta → return link broken, each day's return distribution preserved), 1,000
permutations (20 seeds × 50). A real beta signal ⇒ observed in the far **right** tail.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed BAB | **+1.31 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | **+2.573 bps** (0.728) |
| position of observed | ≈ **1.74σ into the LEFT tail** (right-tail p = 0.991) |

The real beta-sorted book earns **less** than a random assignment into the same leverage cage.
The `1/β_L` scaling on the low-vol leg mechanically manufactures a positive number from *any*
asset placed there (placebo mean +2.57 bps); selecting the genuinely low-beta ETF is a
*below-average* choice, the **opposite** of the Frazzini-Pedersen claim. **The beta signal adds
no value** — the headline positive is levered carry, not a low-risk alpha.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | BAB | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,760) | +0.32 bps | **+0.49** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | +2.13 bps | **+2.68** |

The effect is **entirely a 2018–2026 phenomenon**; the first eight years are flat. Not a
stable, all-weather premium.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

One-way cost × turnover of the levered weights; short leg pays 50 bps/yr borrow. (Financing the
~5× gross leverage at the short rate is **not** charged — with `rf≈0` the levered carry is
flattered; a realistic financing rate erodes what little remains.)

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | borrow/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +1.31 bps | 0.02 bps | 0.11 bps | **+1.19 bps** | +2.14 | 0.55 | +3.0%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +1.31 bps | 0.08 bps | 0.11 bps | **+1.13 bps** | +2.03 | 0.52 | +2.8%/yr |

The friction is small (the beta signal turns over slowly), so the net stays ~3%/yr with net
*t* ≈ 2 — but that number is the placebo-condemned levered carry, confined to one era, and it
survives only because the ~5× leverage is financed for free. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded five-asset curve with a monotone β ladder and a planted low-beta alpha
(`edge>0` ⇒ low β carries positive alpha; `edge=0` = the null). No network.

| world | BAB NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.42** (sd 1.08), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.0015`, seed 826) | **+30.79** (Welch *t* = +15.10, residual β = +0.006) |

The detector recovers a *planted* Frazzini-Pedersen alpha cleanly with a beta-neutral book, and
almost never fires on the null — so the real-tape non-result is a genuine absence of the beta
signal, not a broken engine. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of
the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Frazzini-Pedersen low-risk / BAB alpha does **not** replicate inside
  the Treasury curve. The book prints **+1.31 bps/day** (NW *t* = **+2.50**, right sign) — but
  the permutation placebo shows the beta sort earns *less* than random assignment into the same
  `1/β` cage (observed +1.31 vs placebo +2.57 bps, ≈1.74σ into the left tail), and it is
  entirely a 2018–2026 phenomenon (*t* = +0.49 / +2.68). The clean 20-seed synthetic control
  confirms the machinery is sound; the beta *signal* simply adds nothing, and the headline
  positive is mechanical levered carry.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** What remains is ~3%/yr net (net *t* ≈ 2.1 at 1–5 bps costs) but it
  rests on ~5× gross leverage financed at `rf≈0`, is beaten by random assignment, and lives in
  one era — a mirage, not a harvestable low-risk premium.
